findings.title: Bool variable declarations recorded as TYPE_INT instead of TYPE_BOOL (copy-paste bug)
findings.description: In parser::parse_type_mark(std::string, int) the T_BOOL_TYPE branch correctly calls add_procedure_valid_inputs(...,TYPE_BOOL,...) for context==0 and update_procedure_return_type(...,TYPE_BOOL,...) for context==1, but for context==2 (plain variable/parameter declaration data type) it calls update_identifier_data_type(identifier_name, TYPE_INT, current_scope_id) instead of TYPE_BOOL. Every 'variable x : bool' (and bool procedure parameter) declaration therefore has TYPE_INT recorded as its data type in both the SymbolTable::map and the owning ScopeTable, which will corrupt any later type checking against that identifier (e.g. Typechecker switches on identifier_data_type).

findings.title: token::identifier_data_type has no default initializer -> read as indeterminate garbage
findings.description: Every other data member of `token` has an in-class initializer (type=0, scope_id=0, identifer_type=I_NONE, etc.) except `data_types identifier_data_type;`, which is left uninitialized. Tokens are frequently default-constructed and then only partially filled in (e.g. scanner::build_string_token's fresh `new token`, SymbolTable::insert_stringValue's `new token`, and multiple 'else' branches in SymbolTable.cpp that build a default `token token_to_update;` and never set identifier_data_type before it is read). Typechecker.cpp repeatedly does `switch (first_token.identifier_data_type)` / `switch(token_to_convert.identifier_data_type)` on tokens that may never have had this field set, which is undefined behavior / nondeterministic control flow.

findings.title: Global-scope lookup takes priority over local scope, breaking spec-mandated local shadowing of globals
findings.description: SymbolTable::token_is_in_global_scope(token, int scope_id) ignores its scope_id parameter entirely and only checks scope_table[-1]. It is used as the FIRST branch condition (before any local-scope check) in update_identifier_type (line 265), update_identifier_data_type (line 349), add_procedure_valid_inputs (line 304) and update_procedure_return_type (line 392). In all four functions, when a name already exists in the global pseudo-scope, the caller-supplied local token (with its freshly-parsed identifer_type/data type) is discarded and replaced by whatever is currently stored globally (via get_globabl_token), only patching .scope_id. This means declaring a local variable/procedure that happens to share a name with an existing global does not create an independent local entry - it silently overwrites/reads the *global* entry instead of shadowing it. spec2023.txt section 1.4 explicitly requires: 'Local names can also shadow (or overload) a global name. Hence for the local scope, any reference to that name will denote a reference to the local name and not the global name.' The lookup order here is inverted relative to that requirement (global checked before local).

findings.title: Outermost-scope declarations are not implicitly global unless the 'global' keyword is written, contradicting spec 1.3
findings.description: spec2023.txt section 1.3 states: 'All variables/procedures defined in the outermost scope (of program) are in the global scope (independent of the presence/absence of the global reserved word).' In parse_base_declaration, `is_global_declaration` is only set true inside the `if (Current_parse_token_type == T_GLOBAL)` branch (line 369-372); the `else` branch (no 'global' keyword, lines 402-430) always parses with is_global=false, even when current_scope_id==0 (the outermost program scope). Neither parse_variable_declaration nor parse_procedure_header special-case current_scope_id==0 (grep of parser.cpp for 'current_scope_id == 0' finds no matches), so make_token_global()/scope_table[-1] is never populated for outermost declarations that omit the 'global' keyword, meaning such identifiers are not treated as global as the spec requires.

findings.title: resync_tables returns early from its scope-propagation loop, skipping later scopes/global-sync on first insertion
findings.description: resync_tables builds list_of_scopes (up to 2 entries for I_PROCEDURE tokens: [scope_id, scope_id-1]) and iterates it, but the 'not yet in table' branch does `scope_table[current_scope].insert_string_token(token_to_sync); return true;` - an unconditional return from inside the for-loop. If the token is new in the FIRST scope visited, the function exits before processing any remaining scopes in list_of_scopes, and also before reaching the trailing `if (token_to_sync.global_scope) { scope_table[-1].scope_map[...] = token_to_sync; }` block at line 223-226. For a freshly-declared procedure this means the very first resync call (from update_identifier_type in parse_procedure_header) inserts the procedure name only into its own (child) scope and NOT into the parent scope (scope_id-1) in that call. In the observed call sequence this is masked because parse_procedure_header always immediately follows with parse_type_mark(...,1) -> update_procedure_return_type, whose second resync call finds the name already present in the child scope (so it falls into the non-early-return 'else' branch and reaches i=1/parent). However this self-healing depends on that exact two-call ordering; any call path where update_identifier_data_type/update_procedure_return_type/add_procedure_valid_inputs is invoked for a name not previously registered via update_identifier_type in that scope will hit the same early return and skip the global-scope resync entirely.

findings.title: Scanner resolves every identifier occurrence through the flat, scope-unaware SymbolTable::map, so re-declaring a locally-scoped name that was previously used elsewhere inherits stale payload (e.g. procedure_params)
findings.description: scanner::build_string_token resolves every identifier token via the single flat map keyed only by string (`symbol_table.map[build_string]`), which is last-write-wins across the whole program with no scope awareness. Per spec 1.4, local procedure/variable names can legally be reused across different (sibling) scopes. When a name previously used for one procedure (with accumulated procedure_params written to map[name] by add_procedure_valid_inputs at SymbolTable.cpp:328) is later reused as the name of a *different*, unrelated local procedure in a new scope, Current_parse_token for the new declaration is fetched from map[name] and still carries the *old* procedure's procedure_params vector (parser.cpp never clears .procedure_params before calling update_identifier_type in parse_procedure_header, see parser.cpp:472-476). Because update_identifier_type inserts this stale token into the brand-new (previously-empty) scope table via SymbolTable.cpp:207/278, subsequent add_procedure_valid_inputs calls for the *new* procedure's real parameters find the name 'already in scope table' (SymbolTable.cpp:318-324) and simply push_back onto the pre-populated (stale) procedure_params list instead of clearing it (clearing only happens in the 'not yet in scope table' branch at SymbolTable.cpp:311-317, which this path bypasses) - corrupting the new procedure's recorded parameter signature with leftover types from an unrelated earlier declaration.
findings.evidence:
scanner.cpp:442-451: if (symbol_table.is_in_table(build_string)) { *Current_token = symbol_table.map[build_string]; ... } else { symbol_table.insert_stringValue(build_string, T_IDENTIFIER); *Current_token = symbol_table.map[build_string]; ... }
SymbolTable.cpp:311-324 (add_procedure_valid_inputs): else if (!token_is_in_scope_table(procedure_name, scope_id)) { procedure_identifier_token = map[procedure_name]; ...procedure_params.clear(); } else { temp_scope_map = scope_table[scope_id].scope_map; procedure_identifier_token = temp_scope_map[procedure_name]; procedure_identifier_token.scope_id = scope_id; }

findings.title: Assigning to / referencing an undeclared identifier silently auto-vivifies a blank scope entry instead of erroring
findings.description: parser::update_context_token(token) is called unguarded (no prior is_in_table check) at several sites, e.g. parse_base_statement for assignment-statement destinations (line 1487). It does `Lexer->symbol_table.scope_table[current_scope_id].scope_map[token_to_get_context.stringValue]` using unordered_map::operator[], which auto-creates a default-constructed (blank/garbage, see token.h:126 finding) token entry keyed by that name if it is not already present, rather than signaling 'identifier not found'. Combined with the fact that no 'undeclared identifier' diagnostic exists anywhere in the codebase (grep of parser.cpp/Typechecker.cpp for undeclared/not-defined-style messages returns nothing), this means assigning to a name that was never declared is not detected as an error at the symbol-table level - it silently manufactures an entry with indeterminate identifier_data_type that flows into check_assignment_statement.

findings.title: ScopeTable::insert_string_token silently drops tokens whose .type is not T_IDENTIFIER; default-constructed tokens built in some SymbolTable 'not found' branches never set .type
findings.description: ScopeTable::insert_string_token only stores the token into scope_map if new_token.type == T_IDENTIFIER; otherwise the call is a silent no-op that still returns true. SymbolTable::update_identifier_data_type's 'else' branch (SymbolTable.cpp:365-371) and update_procedure_return_type's 'else' branch (SymbolTable.cpp:405-410) each build a fresh, default-constructed `token token_to_update;` (whose .type defaults to 0, not T_IDENTIFIER) and pass it straight to scope_table[scope_id].insert_string_token(token_to_update) without ever setting .type. In the mainline declaration flow this path appears to be unreachable because update_identifier_type always registers the name (with a real T_IDENTIFIER token from the scanner) in that scope first, but any call path where update_identifier_data_type/update_procedure_return_type is invoked for a name not previously seeded in that exact scope (e.g. parser.cpp:3122 `parse_parameter_list("ERROR")` during error resync, or other resync/error-recovery paths) will silently fail to insert the identifier into the scope table while still returning true, masking the failure from callers.
findings.evidence:
ScopeTable.cpp: bool ScopeTable::insert_string_token(token new_token) { if (new_token.type == T_IDENTIFIER) { ... scope_map[key_value] = new_token; } return 1; }
SymbolTable.cpp:365-371 (update_identifier_data_type else branch): token_to_update.scope_id = scope_id; token_to_update.identifier_data_type = data_type; scope_table[scope_id].insert_string_token(token_to_update);

findings.title: update_scopes(false) has no bounds check; a mismatched 'end procedure' could decrement current_scope_id to -1, colliding with the reserved global pseudo-scope
findings.description: parser::update_scopes(false) unconditionally calls remove_scope(current_scope_id), then decrements current_scope_id and number_of_scopes, with no guard against current_scope_id already being 0. If parser error-recovery (resync_parser) ever allows an unmatched 'end procedure' to be processed at the outermost scope (current_scope_id==0), remove_scope(0) would erase the entire program-level ScopeTable (all top-level declarations), and current_scope_id would become -1 - the same id used for the dedicated global pseudo-scope (SymbolTable.cpp:139,149,225 etc.), causing subsequent local-scope operations to read/write the global table. I did not trace resync_parser's full state machine to confirm this is reachable from malformed input, so this is reported as a design gap rather than a confirmed reachable crash.

findings.title: Tolower_string relies on ::tolower(char) with a potentially-signed char, UB for non-ASCII bytes
findings.description: std::transform(..., ::tolower) passes each char (signed on most platforms, e.g. x86-64 Linux/g++) directly to ::tolower(int), which is only well-defined for values representable as unsigned char or EOF; a byte >=0x80 sign-extends to a negative int, which is undefined behavior for tolower per the C standard. Likely low real-world impact if the scanner only ever admits ASCII letters/digits/underscore into build_string (scanner.cpp:422 gates on isalpha/isdigit/'_' which have the same signed-char caveat), but it's a latent correctness/robustness issue in the identifier-normalization routine explicitly called out for review.

findings.title: ScopeTable::table_scope_id is set only via the parameterized constructor but many call sites auto-vivify ScopeTable via operator[] using the default constructor, leaving it uninitialized garbage (dead field, currently unused)
findings.description: ScopeTable's default constructor (ScopeTable.cpp:3-5) does not initialize table_scope_id, and SymbolTable.cpp repeatedly indexes scope_table[id] via unordered_map::operator[] (e.g. resync_tables line 184 `scope_table[scope_id].procedure_token = ...` before the scope_map_exists/create_new_scope_table check on line 198-201, and token_is_in_global_scope/get_globabl_token/token_is_in_scope_table), which silently default-constructs a ScopeTable bypassing the ScopeTable(int scope_id) constructor used by create_new_scope_table. grep across the repo shows table_scope_id is never read anywhere, so this is currently harmless, but it means the field cannot be trusted if any future code starts relying on it.
findings.evidence:
ScopeTable.cpp: ScopeTable::ScopeTable() {}
SymbolTable.cpp:184 (inside resync_tables, before the scope_map_exists check at line 198): scope_table[scope_id].procedure_token = token_to_sync;

notes:
Scope covered: SymbolTable.cpp/.h, ScopeTable.cpp/.h, CustomFunctions.cpp/.h, token.h, and every parser.cpp/Typechecker.cpp call site that mutates or reads the symbol/scope tables (grep-verified call sites for create_new_scope_table, remove_scope, resync_tables, update_token_scope_id, update_identifier_type, update_identifier_data_type, add_procedure_valid_inputs, update_procedure_return_type, make_token_global, is_global_token, token_is_in_global_scope, get_globabl_token, token_is_in_scope_table, scope_map_exists, insert_string_token, update_scopes, update_context_token). Cross-referenced spec2023.txt sections 1.2-1.4 (case-insensitivity, global-scope rules, local shadowing) and section 2 (builtin I/O functions).

Deliberately NOT re-reported as new findings (already documented verbatim in the repo's own CLAUDE.md, confirmed via a fresh read but omitted per instructions not to parrot known issues): (1) SymbolTable::create_new_scope_table (SymbolTable.cpp:166-172) is missing a return statement - confirmed independently, but its two call sites (SymbolTable.cpp:200, 254) never use the return value, so no live UB is currently triggered; (2) scope-id reuse via number_of_scopes decrementing in parser::update_scopes - I traced this and, under strict LIFO/recursive-descent parsing, current_scope_id always equals nesting depth and scope_id-1 always correctly identifies the immediate parent even after ids are reused by later siblings, so I found no concrete corruption from reuse itself (the related-but-distinct issue I did report is the flat SymbolTable::map being name-keyed and scope-unaware, independent of the -1 global pseudo-scope mechanics); (3) the -1 global pseudo-scope's existence/lookup special-casing is documented as a fact in CLAUDE.md - what I add beyond that doc is the specific, confirmed *precedence inversion* bug (global checked/preferred before local in four update functions) that violates spec 1.4's shadowing rule, and the separate spec-1.3 violation (outermost scope not implicitly global without the keyword); (4) built-in I/O procedures (getInteger/putInteger/etc.) and sqrt not being predeclared is explicitly called out already in CLAUDE.md ("they are not predeclared anywhere") - I independently confirmed this (zero matches for these names anywhere in the C++ sources) but did not re-report it as a primary finding since it would be pure repetition; I instead focused on the SymbolTable-seeding mechanism (init_reserved_words/init_reserved_chars) which is complete for the *keyword* set defined in the grammar (program/is/begin/end/global/procedure/variable/type/integer/float/string/bool/enum/if/then/else/for/return/not/true/false all present) - the gap is specifically the builtin *procedure* predeclaration, already known.

All findings above were derived from direct reading of SymbolTable.cpp, ScopeTable.cpp, token.h, CustomFunctions.cpp, and the relevant parser.cpp call sites (with line numbers cited), plus targeted greps to verify absence of compensating logic (e.g. no "current_scope_id == 0" special-case, no "undeclared identifier" diagnostic, no builtin-function name references anywhere). Several findings involve multi-step call-chain reasoning (e.g., the map-staleness/procedure_params-contamination and the resync_tables early-return self-healing) that I traced through the actual code paths but did not verify by compiling/running a concrete test program against the compiler, so I marked the ultimate observable-behavior consequence as speculative:true while keeping the underlying code-level facts (quoted) as directly confirmed.
